verses.1: In that day there will be a source opened for the house of David and for the inhabitants of Jerusalem, for atonement and for purification.
verses.2: And it will come to pass in that day, says the LORD of Hosts, that I will remove the names of the idols from the land, and they will no longer be remembered. And I will drive out the prophets and the spirit of impurity from the land.
verses.3: And it will come to pass that if any man still prophesies, his father and mother who bore him will say to him, “You must not live, for you have spoken a lie in the name of the LORD.” And his father and mother who bore him will pierce him when he prophesies.
verses.4: And in that day the prophets will be put to shame for their vision when they prophesy, and they will not wear the haircloth of mourning to deceive.
verses.5: And he will say, “I am not a prophet, I am a man who tills the soil, for a man fathered me from my youth.”
verses.6: And someone will ask him, “What are these wounds between your hands?” And he will say, “The wounds I received in the house of my beloved.”
verses.7: Strike the shepherd, and the man who is at my side, says the LORD of Hosts. Strike the shepherd and scatter the flock, and I will turn my hand against the little ones.
verses.8: And it will come to pass in all the land, says the LORD, that two-thirds in it will be struck down and perish, and one-third will remain in it.
verses.9: And I will bring the one-third into the fire, and refine them as silver is refined, and test them as gold is tested. Then they will call upon my name, and I will answer them. I will say, “They are my people,” and they will say, “The LORD is our God.”

notes:
Notes  
- v. 1: "atonement and for purification" — the Hebrew *chatta'at* and *nedah* are both terms for ritual cleansing or purification, often in the context of sin and uncleanness.  
- v. 2: "spirit of impurity" — the Hebrew *ruach ha-tum'ah* is a rare phrase; the context suggests a malevolent or deceptive spiritual force.  
- v. 7: "the man who is at my side" — the Hebrew *gever amithi* is often translated as "companion" or "friend," but the context suggests a political or military leader.  
- v. 8-9: "two-thirds" and "one-third" — the division is symbolic and prophetic, not literal. The Septuagint reads differently in some details, but the Hebrew is clear.
